uncited: Finite difference stencils compute the spatial gradient vector $\nabla V$ of a scalar volume field $V$ by approximating partial derivatives using discrete differences between neighboring voxel values.
This family solves the problem of estimating surface normals and edge strength for volume rendering without requiring analytic derivatives or precomputed gradient volumes.

All methods in this family approximate the partial derivative $\frac{\partial V}{\partial x_i}$ at a voxel center $\mathbf{p}$ using a linear combination of scalar field values $V(\mathbf{p}_k)$ at neighboring positions $\mathbf{p}_k$.
where $w_k$ are weights determined by the stencil geometry and step size $h$ (voxel spacing).
For isotropic grids with $h=1$, the weights are typically integers or simple fractions.
The gradient vector is assembled as $\nabla V = (G_x, G_y, G_z)$.
The family encompasses standard finite difference approximations for gradient computation.
